blockers.description: Actual torch.ones(4,device=cuda) fails in Torch2.11.0+cpu; torch.version.hip/cuda are null. No HIP/HSA runtime found. Vulkan compute success does not supply a PyTorch/LibTorch GPU backend.
remedies: A missing user-space HIP/HSA stack is established; a kernel-driver replacement is NOT_ESTABLISHED. The current ROCm10.1 matrix and targeted gfx1201 Python wheels provide an isolated user-space option using the existing driver, with driver-family compatibility and storage fit still unverified. See gpu-remedies.md/gpu-remedies.json before selecting a separate isolated installation.
Alternatively implement and validate a Vulkan tensor backend with equivalent operations and numerical contracts; present it as a different backend and retain unsupported language bindings.

blockers.description: Standalone Python/native ATen paths work, but CGx2 managed SDK packaging, authenticated dependency closure and emitted native runtime were not built in this frozen-source readiness lane; CGx2 no-libpython claim is NOT_PROVEN.
remedies: Use this pinned native library root to construct an explicit isolated CGx2 SDK/package closure and run the existing native integration acceptance checks in a separately owned implementation task.
Verify its own executable dependency closure and runtime maps; do not infer whole-package Python independence from the standalone ATen smoke.

blockers.description: clGetPlatformIDs returns CL_PLATFORM_NOT_FOUND_KHR(-1001), zero platforms and no /etc/OpenCL/vendors ICDs. OpenCL loader existence is insufficient.
remedies: If an OpenCL comparison is needed, select a GPU-supported Mesa Rusticl or ROCm OpenCL implementation and configure its ICD under an approved separate setup; rerun device identity and compute checks. Vulkan route already works.

blockers.description: Mesa26.2.4 RADV executes the smoke, but emits non-conformant/testing-use warning; hardware readiness alone does not establish production driver or CGx2 backend acceptance.
remedies: Keep this warning in comparisons and pin the driver. For production claims use a validated/conformant GPU driver release in a separately approved environment and rerun the smoke and workload correctness.
